ruling.recommended_action: Issue rider a $5.10 Ryde voucher (metered distance overcharge for the un-exempted detour past the Seletar Expressway accident); note the driver's RD-1 breach (metered distance 19.31 km vs quoted 17.253 km) on file. No account flag (no prior upheld route dispute in 90 days).

segment_findings.reason: Deviation from the quoted route starting near the SLE approach (approx. 17:32–17:38, GPS heading west past 103.808 then 103.813–103.814) taken to bypass the Seletar Expressway accident. LTA incident 'Accident on Seletar Expressway (towards Punggol Waterway Point)', reported 17:16, lies on the quoted route polyline within the 300 m matching radius and was still active during the trip window, so the 'reasonable cause' exception in RD-4(a) applies → exempt, no refund for this segment.

Closed loop off the quoted route around Seletar/Tampines (approx. 17:41–17:44: 1.3952,103.8325 → 1.4019,103.8276 → back to 1.3952,103.8327), roughly 1.5–1.7 km of doubling back. This is not the route past the accident and no traffic incident or band-1/2 record supports it (RD-4(b) alone does not exempt); no pre-deviation chat agreement satisfies RD-5. It is an un-exempted detour and its extra_km enters the RD-2 metered-distance refund.

rejected_claims.reason: Partially rejected. The accident was real and on-route (RD-4(a) exempts the SLE bypass), but it does not explain the ~1.5–1.7 km closed loop taken around Seletar/Tampines after the bypass; that portion of the extra distance remains chargeable and refundable under RD-2.

Accepted as to fact (no chat consent exists, RD-5), but the first deviation is nonetheless exempt on reasonable-cause grounds (RD-4(a)), so the rider is not entitled to a refund of the entire quoted-vs-metered difference.
